title: Registration submit contract
description: D18 addendum rule 6 (execution plan §2.6.1; queue item SPEC-REG-NEGOTIATE). A controller submits its controller-owned registration (controller-state-model.schema.json) to the `submit.href` its hub publishes in the capability document (hub-capabilities.schema.json), reads back per element what was accepted, and writes the well-known carrier for anything not accepted. One registration per tenant per identity (`metadata.vendor`, `metadata.product`) is the resource `<submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>`: `PUT` submits or updates it, `GET` reads it with its current element results, `DELETE` retires it. This file defines the request as the conformance fixtures model it, the response, the controller's fallback, and the conformance case (specs/sync/conformance/). The prose contract, including the open questions, is in the hub-sync design §3.5. Must-ignore applies: no object is closed, and a controller treats an element result or reason code it does not know as not accepted.

identity.description: A registration's identity within a tenant: `metadata.vendor` and `metadata.product`. `versionRange` is an attribute of the registration, not part of its identity: a new controller release updates the same registration and keeps older served versions under rule 4.

etag.description: The registration's entity tag: `sha256:` and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of `{"registration": <the registration as submitted>, "state": <state>}`. It changes whenever the stored registration or its state changes and never on a no-op. Sent and compared as an HTTP strong entity tag (quoted on the wire).

request.description: One request, as the fixtures model it. `submit` is `PUT <submit.href>/<vendor>/<product>` with the registration as the body; `retire` is `DELETE` on the same resource with no body. Every request carries exactly one precondition: `ifNoneMatch: "*"` to create, `ifMatch: <etag>` to update or retire. A request with none is answered 428 (`precondition-required`), so no update is ever blind.

reason.description: Why a registration or an element was not accepted, or why a request changed nothing. `code` is an open vocabulary (rule 3): a hub uses `other` with its own `term` for a reason not listed, and a controller treats any reason it does not know as not accepted.

term.description: The hub's own term, when `code` is `other`.

path.description: The dotted path in the registration the reason is about, in the form tools/nsschema/sync_model.py `unknown_grammar_fields` uses.

detail.description: Human-readable. A controller must not parse it.

elementResult.description: The result for one element of a stored registration. Elements: `stateSpans/<kind or category>`, `extensions/<namespace>`, `settings.fields/<name>` and `replayInputs/<input>` (the last two for typed fields only). `accepted-with-ignored-members`: accepted, and the listed members of the element are ignored (rule 1). `rejected`: the hub offers no typed API for the element; the controller writes its well-known carrier.

response.description: The hub's answer to a submit, retire or read. `outcome`: `accepted` (stored; every element accepted, possibly with ignored members), `partial` (stored; at least one element rejected), `rejected` (nothing stored or changed; `reasons` says why), `precondition-failed` (nothing changed; `current` carries the stored etag and state), `not-found` (nothing stored under this identity), `retired` (the registration is retired; stored data is kept). `noop`: the request asked for what was already stored, so nothing changed and the etag is the stored one (a retried create or update succeeds; RFC 9110 §13.1.1 allows a 2xx for If-Match when the requested change has already been applied, and this contract applies the same rule to a create's If-None-Match).

status.description: The HTTP status. 201 created; 200 updated, retired, read or no-op; 403 the credential may not do this; 404 not found; 412 a precondition failed; 413 too large; 422 rejected for its content; 428 no precondition sent.

registration.description: The stored registration's identity, state and etag after the request. Absent when nothing is stored.

current.description: With `precondition-failed`: what is stored now, so the controller can read it and resubmit.

reasons.description: Registration-level reasons: why the request was rejected or changed nothing.

ignored.description: Rule 1. Members outside any element that the hub ignores, as dotted paths.

fallbackEntry.description: What the controller writes for one element. `typed`: through the typed API the hub derived. `carrier`: the element's well-known carrier (`stateSpans[].wire`, or an extension's `carrier`), as today's documents. `untyped`: a typed setting or replay input is written where it is today and the hub treats it as name-only. `none`: the element has no well-known carrier, so the hub receives nothing for it.

fallback.description: The controller's write plan, one entry per element of its registration, keyed by element id.

conformanceCase.description: One conformance case (specs/sync/conformance/*.yaml): a hub's capability document and stored state, a submitter, a controller's registration and request, and the expected response and controller fallback. All content is synthetic. A hub implementation passes a case when, booted with `capabilities` and `hubState` and sent `request` with `registration` by a credential holding `submitter`, it answers `expected.response` (reason `detail` strings are not compared) and stores `expected.storedAfter` where the case states it.

control.description: For a case whose request is rejected, fails a precondition or rejects an element: the id of the passing case that differs from it only in the aspect under test.

cell.description: The D18 addendum compatibility cell this case exercises.

capabilities.description: The hub's capability document. null: the hub publishes none (an older hub; `/.well-known/nightscout/sync` answers 404).

wellKnownRegistrations.description: The well-known registrations the capability document links to, keyed by `href`.

submitter.description: What the submitting credential holds on this tenant: its permissions (shiro-style, `*` a wildcard part) and the namespace roots it may claim. How a credential comes to hold namespace roots is an open question (hub-sync design §3.5); the case states the outcome given them.

registration.description: The controller's registration. null: an older controller that has none.

grammarValid.description: Whether `registration` validates against controller-state-model.schema.json. Stated so a case cannot pass by testing an invalid registration where a valid one was meant.

writes.description: For an older controller: documents it writes today, to show which well-known registration describes each.

controllerWouldSubmit.description: Whether a controller following the contract submits at all, given the capability document: it does when the document exists, offers `submit`, and lists its grammar major. A case may still send a request the controller would not, to test the hub.

describedBy.description: For `writes`: the well-known registration (and element, when a kind's wire carrier matches) that describes each write.

storedAfter.description: The stored registration after the request, or null when none is stored.
